central_question: Over 2026-2031, how will Modern Mercantilism and the AI capital/compute buildout co-evolve, and who wins and who loses as tariffs, export controls, sovereign compute, and the AI capex supercycle collide?

situation_brief.current_situation: As of mid-2026 two structural regimes have locked in simultaneously: a durable elevated-tariff regime (US effective tariff rate settled just above 11% by April 2026 after the Feb 20 2026 SCOTUS ruling struck down IEEPA tariffs and the administration pivoted to Section 122/232/301) and an AI capex/compute-scarcity regime (Big-4 hyperscalers guiding to ~$700-725B in 2026 capex, up ~77% from 2025). AI compute is now simultaneously a mercantilist weapon (export-controlled chips) and a mercantilist prize (courted data-center capacity, contested rare-earth/energy inputs). A one-year US-China truce suspends new rare-earth controls through Nov 27 2026, while the US permits licensed advanced-chip sales to China via a 25% revenue-share model.
situation_brief.context: US-China tech decoupling (2018-2024) produced escalating chip export controls answered by Chinese gallium/germanium and rare-earth weaponization. Trump's second term brought Stargate ($500B), Liberation Day reciprocal tariffs (Apr 2025, ETR peak ~28%), DeepSeek's efficient open model (Jan 2025) disconfirming compute-hoarding, and a flip of the H20 chip from banned to approved to revenue-shared within 2025. TSMC raised its US commitment to $165B; the Oct-Nov 2025 Trump-Xi truce moved the relationship from open escalation to managed interdependence.
situation_brief.dynamics: Forces in tension: efficiency vs. security; compute abundance vs. compute rationing; decoupling vs. mutual chokepoint hostage-taking (US->rare earths, China->advanced tools); a ~$700B/yr capex boom vs. uncertain ROI and bond-market financing strain; open-weight diffusion undercutting the value of closed-model hoarding and export bans. The AI buildout is financed in the same bond market straining under US deficits, creating a self-imposed 18-36 month monetization deadline that slow AI diffusion may not meet.
fault_lines: Do export controls work, or do they accelerate an indigenous Chinese stack (SMIC/Huawei/DeepSeek) and hand China the open-model lead?
Is the AI capex boom a productivity supercycle or a bubble whose unwind triggers a market/credit event?
Who bears tariff incidence - foreign exporters (mercantilist claim) or domestic consumers/firms (Budget Lab evidence)?
Can the US reshore advanced fabrication fast enough (leading-edge is a ~2030 story) before a Taiwan contingency?
Does AI net-create or net-destroy jobs during a tariff-driven cost shock, and how concentrated are the gains?
Can the West build a non-China rare-earth/magnet supply chain within the horizon, or does China retain a coercive veto?
catalysts: Resolution of IEEPA tariff refund mechanics and any Section 232 semiconductor tariff finalization
Nov 27 2026 rare-earth truce expiry becoming a scheduled flashpoint
An AI-capex financing stress event (>=$10B buildout cancellation or >150bps AI credit-spread blowout)
A DeepSeek-scale efficiency shock resetting the compute-scarcity thesis
A Taiwan military/coercion event disrupting TSMC output
A US-China grand bargain institutionalizing managed interdependence (chips-for-minerals + market access)
